# go/types can only read export data written by the Go release it was built
# with, and the simd package can change in a patch release without go/types
# seeing it (go1.27.0 compiles ShiftAllRight as taking a uint8). When
# loopvec-toolexec was built with a different Go version than the toolchain
# running the build, patch included, packages are compiled unchanged, and the
# log (with LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_DEBUG) says why.

chmod 0755 compile patch/compile
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_DEBUG=1
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG=$WORK/log
exec $LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC $WORK/compile -p example.com/x -importcfg $WORK/b001/importcfg x.go
cmpenv stdout stdout.want
! stderr .
stdout -count=1 '^fake compile: '
grep -count=1 '^skipped example\.com/x: loopvec-toolexec was built with go1\.[^ ]+ but the toolchain is go1\.1$' log

# Same release, another patch.
exec $LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC $WORK/patch/compile -p example.com/y -importcfg $WORK/b001/importcfg x.go
stdout -count=1 '^fake compile: -p example\.com/y '
! stderr .
grep -count=1 '^skipped example\.com/y: loopvec-toolexec was built with go1\.[^ ]+ but the toolchain is go1\.27\.0$' log

-- compile --
#!/bin/sh
if [ "$1" = "-V=full" ]; then
	echo "compile version go1.1 X:simd"
	exit 0
fi
echo "fake compile: $@"
-- patch/compile --
#!/bin/sh
if [ "$1" = "-V=full" ]; then
	echo "compile version go1.27.0 X:simd"
	exit 0
fi
echo "fake compile: $@"
-- x.go --
package x
-- stdout.want --
fake compile: -p example.com/x -importcfg $WORK/b001/importcfg x.go
